title.zh: 卷七十五 劉焉袁術吕布列傳
title.en: Volume 75: Biographies of Liu Yan, Yuan Shu, Lü Bu
title.raw: 卷七十五 劉焉袁術吕布列傳 Volume 75: Biographies of Liu Yan, Yuan Shu, Lü Bu

sentences.zh: 劉焉字君郎，江夏竟陵人也，魯恭王後也。

translations.literal: Liu Yan, courtesy name Junlang, was a man of Jingling in Jiangxia, and a descendant of Prince Gong of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan, styled Junlang, came from Jingling in Jiangxia and traced his line to Prince Gong of Lu.

sentences.zh: 肅宗時，徙竟陵。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Suzong, the family was relocated to Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Suzong his clan was moved to Jingling.

sentences.zh: 焉少任州郡，以宗室拜郎中。

translations.literal: In youth Yan held office in the provinces and commanderies, and as a member of the imperial clan was appointed Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he served in provincial posts and, by virtue of his imperial lineage, received appointment as a Gentleman of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 去官居陽城山，精學教授。

translations.literal: Leaving office, he dwelt on Mount Yangcheng, devoted himself to study, and taught.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned, withdrew to Mount Yangcheng, pursued scholarship in earnest, and lectured to students.

sentences.zh: 舉賢良方正，稍遷南陽太守、宗正、太常。

translations.literal: Recommended as Worthy and Good, Honest and Upright, he was gradually promoted to Governor of Nanyang, Minister of the Imperial Clan, and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as an outstanding candidate for honest and upright conduct, he rose step by step to governor of Nanyang, minister for the imperial clan, and minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 時，靈帝政化衰缺，四方兵寇，焉以為刺史威輕，既不能禁，且用非其人，輒增暴亂，乃建議改置牧伯，鎮安方夏，清選重臣，以居其任。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Ling's governance was decaying and flawed; armed bandits arose on every side. Yan held that the inspectors' authority was light: they could neither restrain trouble, and when the wrong men were appointed, violence only increased. He therefore proposed replacing them with regional shepherds, to pacify the realm, and selecting eminent ministers of proven weight to fill those posts.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ling government faltered and rebellion spread. Liu Yan argued that provincial inspectors lacked real authority—unable to keep order, and that wrong appointments only bred more chaos—so he urged installing chief administrators over the regions to stabilize the empire and staffing those offices with senior, carefully chosen ministers.

sentences.zh: 焉乃陰求為交阯，以避時難。

translations.literal: Yan then secretly sought appointment to Jiaozhi, to escape the troubles of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He quietly angled for a posting to Jiaozhi, hoping to ride out the turmoil at a distance.

sentences.zh: 議未即行，會益州刺史郗儉在政煩擾，謠言遠聞，而并州刺史張懿、涼州刺史耿鄙並為寇賊所害，故焉議得用。

translations.literal: The proposal had not yet been carried out when Inspector Xi Jian of Yi Province proved vexatious in administration and rumors of it spread far; moreover Inspectors Zhang Yi of Bing and Geng Bi of Liang were both killed by bandits, so Yan's plan was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Before the reform could take effect, Yi Province's Inspector Xi Jian had drawn widespread complaint for his harsh rule, while the inspectors of Bing and Liang, Zhang Yi and Geng Bi, had both fallen to rebels—circumstances that finally won acceptance for Liu Yan's proposal.

sentences.zh: 出焉為監軍使者，領益州牧，太僕黃琬為豫州牧，宗正劉虞為幽州牧，皆以本秩居職。

translations.literal: Yan was sent out as Military Overseer and Envoy and appointed shepherd of Yi Province; Grand Coachman Huang Wan became shepherd of Yu Province; Minister of the Imperial Clan Liu Yu became shepherd of You Province; each held office at his existing salary rank.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan was named military overseer and shepherd of Yi Province, Huang Wan grand coachman and shepherd of Yu, and Liu Yu minister of the imperial clan and shepherd of You, each continuing at his former nominal grade.

sentences.zh: 州任之重，自此而始。

translations.literal: The weight of responsibility for a province began from this.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment the office of provincial shepherd carried real power.

sentences.zh: 是時，益州賊馬相亦自號「黃巾」，合聚疲役之民數千人，先殺綿竹令，進攻雒縣，殺郗儉，又擊蜀郡、犍為，旬月之間，破壞三郡。

translations.literal: At this time the bandit Ma Xiang in Yi Province also styled himself "Yellow Turban," gathered several thousand exhausted commoners, first killed the magistrate of Mianzhu, advanced to attack Luo County, killed Xi Jian, then struck Shu and Qianwei; within a month or so three commanderies were ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Ma Xiang of Yi Province took the name "Yellow Turban," rallied thousands of worn-down laborers, murdered the magistrate of Mianzhu, took Luo County and killed Xi Jian, then overran Shu and Qianwei—three commanderies collapsed in a matter of weeks.

sentences.zh: 馬相自稱「天子」，眾至十餘萬人，遣兵破巴郡，殺郡守趙部。

translations.literal: Ma Xiang declared himself "Son of Heaven"; his host grew to over a hundred thousand. He sent troops to break Ba commandery and killed the governor Zhao Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiang proclaimed himself "Son of Heaven" and swelled his ranks past a hundred thousand; his forces smashed Ba commandery and executed Governor Zhao Bu.

sentences.zh: 州從事賈龍，先領兵數百人在犍為，遂糾合吏人攻相，破之，龍乃遣吏卒迎焉。

translations.literal: The provincial aide Jia Long had earlier led several hundred soldiers in Qianwei; he then rallied clerks and commoners to attack Xiang and defeated him. Long then sent officers and soldiers to welcome Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial aide Jia Long, already in Qianwei with a few hundred men, rallied officials and locals, routed Ma Xiang, and sent an escort to bring Liu Yan in.

sentences.zh: 焉到，以龍為校尉，徙居綿竹。

translations.literal: When Yan arrived, he appointed Long colonel and moved his residence to Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival Liu Yan made Jia Long a colonel and established his headquarters at Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 撫納離叛，務行寬惠，而陰圖異計。

translations.literal: He soothed and accepted those who had broken away, striving to practice leniency and kindness, while secretly plotting other designs.
translations.idiomatic: He won over defectors with a policy of mild rule, all the while laying secret plans of his own.

sentences.zh: 沛人張魯，母有姿色，兼挾鬼道，往來焉家，遂任魯以為督義司馬，與別部司馬張脩將兵掩殺漢中太守蘇固，斷絕斜谷，殺使者。

translations.literal: Zhang Lu of Pei—his mother was attractive and practiced spirit arts—went back and forth to Yan's household; Yan thereupon appointed Lu chief marshal for righteousness and, with Separate Division Marshal Zhang Xiu, led troops in a surprise attack that killed Su Gu, governor of Hanzhong, cut off the Xie Valley road, and killed the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu of Pei had a mother who was both striking and adept at spirit mediums' practices; she frequented Liu Yan's house, and Liu gave Zhang Lu the post of chief marshal for righteousness. Together with Separate Division Marshal Zhang Xiu he struck Hanzhong, killed Governor Su Gu, sealed the Xie Valley pass, and slew the imperial messenger.

sentences.zh: 魯既得漢中，遂復殺張脩而併其眾。

translations.literal: Once Lu had obtained Hanzhong, he again killed Zhang Xiu and annexed his troops.
translations.idiomatic: After securing Hanzhong, Zhang Lu eliminated Zhang Xiu and absorbed his army.

sentences.zh: 焉欲立威刑以自尊大，乃託以佗事，殺州中豪強十餘人，士民皆怨。

translations.literal: Yan wished to establish awe through punishments to magnify himself; under other pretexts he killed more than ten powerful families of the province, and gentlemen and commoners alike resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking to cow the province and elevate his own stature, Liu Yan trumped up charges and executed over ten leading local families, earning widespread resentment.

sentences.zh: 初平二年，犍為太守任岐及賈龍並反，攻焉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chuping, Ren Qi, governor of Qianwei, and Jia Long together rebelled and attacked Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In 191 Qianwei's governor Ren Qi joined Jia Long in revolt and marched against Liu Yan.

sentences.zh: 焉擊破，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Yan defeated them and killed them both.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan crushed the rising and put both men to death.

sentences.zh: 自此意氣漸盛，遂造作乘輿車重千餘乘。

translations.literal: From this his arrogance gradually swelled, and he then had made over a thousand imperial-style carriages and baggage carts.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened, he grew ambitious enough to commission more than a thousand vehicles fit for an emperor's train.

sentences.zh: 焉四子，範為左中郎將，誕治書御史，璋奉車都尉，並從獻帝在長安，唯別部司馬瑁隨焉在益州。

translations.literal: Yan had four sons: Fan was General of the Gentlemen of the Household for the Left; Dan was Attendant Censor for Documents; Zhang was Commandant of the Carriages and Cavalry; all accompanied Emperor Xian at Chang'an. Only Separate Division Marshal Mao remained with Yan in Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Of Liu Yan's four sons, Fan served as a general of the household left, Dan as document censor, and Zhang as commandant of the imperial equipage—all at Emperor Xian's court in Chang'an—while only Separate Division Marshal Mao stayed with his father in Yi.

sentences.zh: 朝廷使璋曉譬焉，焉留璋不復遣。

translations.literal: The court sent Zhang to reason with Yan; Yan detained Zhang and did not send him back.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched Liu Zhang to talk sense into his father, but Liu Yan kept him in Yi and never let him return.

sentences.zh: 興平元年，征西將軍馬騰與範謀誅李傕，焉遣叟兵五千助之，戰敗，範及誕並見殺。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingping, General Who Conquers the West Ma Teng plotted with Fan to kill Li Jue; Yan sent five thousand tribal soldiers from the southwest to assist them. They were defeated in battle, and Fan and Dan were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: In 194 Ma Teng conspired with Liu Fan to eliminate Li Jue; Liu Yan sent five thousand tribal auxiliaries from the southwest. The venture failed, and both Liu Fan and Liu Dan lost their lives.

sentences.zh: 焉既痛二子，又遇天火燒其城府車重，延及民家，館邑無餘，於是徙居成都，遂疽發背卒。

translations.literal: Yan grieved for his two sons; moreover heaven-sent fire burned his walls, treasury, and baggage carts, spreading to commoners' homes until nothing of his compounds remained. He therefore moved his residence to Chengdu, then died of a carbuncle on his back.
translations.idiomatic: Stricken by his sons' deaths, Liu Yan then watched fire consume his city stores, wagons, and neighborhoods until little was left; he relocated to Chengdu, where a back abscess carried him off.

sentences.zh: 州大吏趙韙等貪璋溫仁，立為刺史。

translations.literal: Senior provincial officers such as Zhao Wei, coveting Zhang's mild kindness, installed him as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Leading officials led by Zhao Wei, liking Liu Zhang's gentle manner, raised him to provincial inspector.

sentences.zh: 詔書因以璋為監軍使者，領益州牧，以韙為征東中郎將。

translations.literal: An edict thereupon made Zhang Military Overseer and Envoy and shepherd of Yi Province, and Wei General of the Household for the East.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial orders named Liu Zhang military overseer and shepherd of Yi, and appointed Zhao Wei general of the household for the east.

sentences.zh: 先是，荊州牧劉表表焉僭擬乘輿器服，韙以此遂屯兵朐䏰備表。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Biao, shepherd of Jing Province, had memorialized that Yan had presumptuously copied imperial carriage gear and vestments; on this account Wei then stationed troops at Qu to guard against Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jing's shepherd Liu Biao had denounced Liu Yan for aping the emperor's regalia; Zhao Wei accordingly garrisoned Qu to watch Liu Biao.

sentences.zh: 初，南陽、三輔民數万戶流入益州，焉悉收以為眾，名曰「東州兵」。

translations.literal: Earlier, several tens of thousands of households from Nanyang and the Three Adjuncts had flowed into Yi Province; Yan gathered them all as a host and named them the "Eastern Province troops."
translations.idiomatic: When tens of thousands of refugees from Nanyang and the capital region poured into Yi, Liu Yan enrolled them wholesale as what he called the "Eastern Province troops."

sentences.zh: 璋性柔寬無威略，東州入侵暴為民患，不能禁制，舊士頗有離怨。

translations.literal: Zhang's nature was soft and indulgent, without stern strategy; the Eastern Province men invaded and acted violently, becoming a plague on the people, and he could not restrain them; the old elite grew alienated and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang was too mild to impose discipline: the Eastern Province troops bullied the locals, he failed to check them, and the established families turned against him.

sentences.zh: 趙韓之在巴中，甚得眾心，璋委之以權。

translations.literal: As for Zhao Han, in Ba he won the hearts of the multitude very much; Zhang entrusted him with authority.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wei held Ba with strong local backing, and Liu Zhang entrusted him with real authority.

sentences.zh: 韙因人情不輯，乃陰結州中大姓。

translations.literal: Because popular feeling was not harmonious, Wei secretly allied with the great clans of the province.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing morale fray, Zhao Wei secretly enlisted the province's leading families.

sentences.zh: 建安五年，還共擊璋，蜀郡、廣漢、犍為皆反應。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jian'an, they together struck Zhang; Shu, Guanghan, and Qianwei all responded in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In 200 they rose jointly against Liu Zhang, and Shu, Guanghan, and Qianwei rose with them.

sentences.zh: 東州人畏見誅滅，乃同心並力，為璋死戰，遂破反者，進攻韙於江州，斬之。

translations.literal: The Eastern Province men feared extermination; they united hearts and strength and fought to the death for Zhang, thereby defeating the rebels, then advanced to attack Wei at Jiangzhou and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing slaughter, the Eastern Province troops closed ranks and fought desperately for Liu Zhang, crushed the revolt, advanced on Zhao Wei at Jiangzhou, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 張魯以璋暗懦，不復承順。

translations.literal: Zhang Lu, considering Zhang dim and timid, no longer obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu treated Liu Zhang as weak and ceased to defer to him.

sentences.zh: 璋怒，殺魯母及弟，而遣其將龐羲等攻魯，數為所破。

translations.literal: Zhang was angry; he killed Lu's mother and younger brother, then sent his generals Pang Xi and others to attack Lu, but was repeatedly defeated by him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang retaliated by executing Zhang Lu's mother and brother and dispatching Pang Xi and others—only to suffer defeat again and again.

sentences.zh: 魯部曲多在巴土，故以羲為巴郡太守。

translations.literal: Lu's lieutenants were mostly in Ba territory, so Xi was made governor of Ba commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhang Lu's forces held Ba, Liu Zhang named Pang Xi governor of Ba commandery.

sentences.zh: 魯因襲取之，遂雄於巴漢。

translations.literal: Lu thereupon surprised him and took it, and thus became powerful in Ba and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu seized the opening and drove him out, thereafter dominating the Ba–Han region.

sentences.zh: 十三年，曹操自將征荊州，璋乃遣使致敬。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Cao Cao personally led a campaign against Jing Province; Zhang thereupon sent envoys to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: In 208 Cao Cao marched on Jing in person; Liu Zhang dispatched envoys to court his favor.

sentences.zh: 操加璋振威將軍，兄瑁平寇將軍。

translations.literal: Cao promoted Zhang to General Who Inspires Awe; his elder brother Mao to General Who Pacifies Bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao named Liu Zhang general who inspires awe and his brother Liu Mao general who pacifies bandits.

sentences.zh: 璋因遣別駕從事張松詣操，而操不相接禮。

translations.literal: Zhang then sent his aide-de-camp Zhang Song to Cao Cao, but Cao did not receive him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang sent deputy Zhang Song to Cao Cao's camp, only to be cold-shouldered.

sentences.zh: 松懷恨而還，勸璋絕曹氏，而結好劉備。

translations.literal: Song harbored resentment and returned, urging Zhang to break with the House of Cao and ally with Liu Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Smarting from the snub, Zhang Song urged Liu Zhang to break with Cao Cao and align with Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 璋從之。

translations.literal: Zhang followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang agreed.

sentences.zh: 十六年，璋聞曹操當遣兵向漢中討張魯，內懷恐懼，松复說璋迎劉備以拒操。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Zhang heard that Cao Cao was about to send troops toward Hanzhong to attack Zhang Lu; inwardly he was afraid. Song again urged Zhang to welcome Liu Bei to resist Cao.
translations.idiomatic: In 211, alarmed that Cao Cao might march on Hanzhong against Zhang Lu, Liu Zhang let Zhang Song talk him into inviting Liu Bei as a counterweight.

sentences.zh: 璋即遣法正將兵迎備。

translations.literal: Zhang immediately sent Fa Zheng to lead troops to welcome Bei.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Fa Zheng with an escort to bring Liu Bei in.

sentences.zh: 璋主簿巴西黃權諫曰：「劉備有梟名，今以部曲遇之，則不滿其心，以賓客待之，則一國不容二主，此非自安之道。

translations.literal: Zhang's registrar, Huang Quan of Ba, remonstrated: Liu Bei has the reputation of an owl. If you treat him as a subordinate leader, you will not satisfy his heart; if you treat him as a guest, one state cannot hold two lords. This is not a way to secure yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Registrar Huang Quan of Ba warned him that Liu Bei was a bird of prey: receive him as a subordinate and you wound his pride; receive him as an honored guest and two masters cannot share one realm—neither course brings safety.

sentences.zh: 」從事廣漢王累自倒懸於州門以諫。

translations.literal: The aide Wang Lei of Guanghan hung himself upside down at the provincial gate to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Aide Wang Lei of Guanghan even hung himself upside down at the provincial gate in protest.

sentences.zh: 璋一無所納。

translations.literal: Zhang accepted none of it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang brushed every warning aside.

sentences.zh: 備自江陵馳至涪城，璋率步騎數万與備會。

translations.literal: Bei galloped from Jiangling to Fucheng; Zhang led several tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry to meet Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei rode hard from Jiangling to Fucheng, where Liu Zhang met him with tens of thousands of horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 張松勸備於會襲璋，備不忍。

translations.literal: Zhang Song urged Bei to strike Zhang at the meeting; Bei could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Song wanted Liu Bei to ambush Liu Zhang at the parley; Liu Bei refused out of scruple.

sentences.zh: 明年，出屯葭萌。

translations.literal: The next year he went out and encamped at Jiameng.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he marched out and camped at Jiameng.

sentences.zh: 松兄廣漢太守肅懼禍及己，乃以松謀白璋，收松斬之，敕諸關戍勿復通。

translations.literal: Song's elder brother Su, governor of Guanghan, feared calamity reaching himself; he therefore informed Zhang of Song's plot, Song was seized and beheaded, and orders went to all passes and garrisons not to communicate further.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Su, governor of Guanghan and Zhang Song's brother, feared implication, he exposed the plot to Liu Zhang; Zhang Song was executed and every border post was ordered sealed.

sentences.zh: 備大怒，還兵擊璋，所在戰克。

translations.literal: Bei was greatly angry; he turned his troops to strike Zhang and wherever he fought he prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Liu Bei turned his army on Liu Zhang and swept every field.

sentences.zh: 十九年，進圍成都，數十日，城中有精兵三萬人，穀支一年，吏民咸欲拒戰。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he advanced and besieged Chengdu. After several tens of days, inside the walls were thirty thousand crack troops and grain enough for a year; clerks and commoners all wished to resist.
translations.idiomatic: In 214 he invested Chengdu. Even after weeks of siege the city still held thirty thousand veterans and a year's grain; officials and townspeople begged to fight on.

sentences.zh: 璋言：「父子在州二十餘歲，無恩德以加百姓，而攻戰三載，肌膏草野者，以璋故也。

translations.literal: Zhang said: "For father and son to sit in this province more than twenty years, we have had no kindness or virtue to give the common people, yet for three years war has raged and those whose flesh and fat grease the grasslands—this is Zhang's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang said, "My father and I have held this land over twenty years without earning the people's goodwill, while three years of fighting have carpeted the fields with corpses—all because of me.

sentences.zh: 何心能安！

translations.literal: What heart could be at peace!
translations.idiomatic: How could my conscience find peace!

sentences.zh: 」遂開城出降，群下莫不流涕。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he opened the gates and came out to surrender; none among his subordinates failed to weep.
translations.idiomatic: " He then opened the gates and submitted, and every man under him wept.

sentences.zh: 備遷璋於公安，歸其財寶，後以病卒。

translations.literal: Bei relocated Zhang to Gong'an, returned his treasures, and later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei moved him to Gong'an, restored his valuables, and Liu Zhang eventually died of illness.

sentences.zh: 明年，曹操破張魯，定漢中。

translations.literal: The next year, Cao Cao defeated Zhang Lu and pacified Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Cao Cao crushed Zhang Lu and brought Hanzhong under control.

sentences.zh: 魯字公旗。

translations.literal: Lu's courtesy name was Gongqi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu, courtesy name Gongqi.

sentences.zh: 初，祖父陵，順帝時客於蜀，學道鶴鳴山中，造作符書，以惑百姓。

translations.literal: Earlier, his grandfather Ling, in the time of Emperor Shun, sojourned in Shu, studied the Way on Mount Heming, fabricated talismanic writings, and thereby deluded the common people.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhang Ling had settled in Shu under Emperor Shun, pursued Daoist arts on Mount Heming, composed spirit talismans, and drew the populace after him.

sentences.zh: 受其道者輒出米五斗，故謂之「米賊」。

translations.literal: Those who received his teaching regularly contributed five pecks of rice, hence they were called the "rice bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Followers paid five pecks of rice as dues, which earned the sect the nickname "rice bandits."

sentences.zh: 陵傳子衡，衡傳於魯，魯遂自號「師君」。

translations.literal: Ling transmitted to his son Heng; Heng transmitted to Lu; Lu thereupon styled himself "Master Lord."
translations.idiomatic: The line passed from Zhang Ling to Zhang Heng and then to Zhang Lu, who proclaimed himself "Master Lord."

sentences.zh: 其來學者，初名為「鬼卒」，後號「祭酒」。

translations.literal: Those who came to study were at first named "ghost soldiers," later titled "libationers."
translations.idiomatic: Neophytes were first called "ghost soldiers," then promoted to "libationers."

sentences.zh: 祭酒各領部眾，眾多者名曰「理頭」。

translations.literal: Each libationer commanded a following; those with many followers were called "heads who govern."
translations.idiomatic: Each libationer led a congregation; the largest were titled "heads of section."

sentences.zh: 皆校以誠信，不聽欺妄，有病但令首過而已。

translations.literal: All were regulated by sincerity and trustworthiness; deceit was not permitted; if ill, they were only made to confess faults.
translations.idiomatic: The community stressed honesty—lies were forbidden—and the sick merely confessed their misdeeds.

sentences.zh: 諸祭酒各起義舍於路，同之亭傳，縣置米肉以給行旅。

translations.literal: The libationers each established righteous lodges along the roads, the same as post stations; counties set out rice and meat to supply travelers.
translations.idiomatic: Libationers built hostels along the highways like imperial relay inns, with counties laying in rice and meat for wayfarers.

sentences.zh: 食者量腹取足，過多則鬼能病之。

translations.literal: Eaters measured belly and took enough; if too much, ghosts could sicken them.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers were told to take only what they needed—greed brought ghost-sent illness.

sentences.zh: 犯法者先加三原，然後行刑。

translations.literal: Those who violated the law were first granted three reprieves, then punishment was applied.
translations.idiomatic: Offenders received three chances to reform before facing sentence.

sentences.zh: 不置長吏，以祭酒為理，民夷信向。

translations.literal: They did not appoint senior officials; libationers acted as administrators, and commoners and tribes alike trusted and inclined toward them.
translations.idiomatic: With no regular magistrates, libationers governed, winning the confidence of Han settlers and native tribes alike.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不能討，遂就拜魯鎮夷中郎將，領漢寧太守。

translations.literal: The court could not subdue them; thereupon it confirmed Lu as General of the Household for Pacifying the Tribes and governor of Hanning.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to suppress him by force, the court instead confirmed Zhang Lu as general for pacifying the tribes and governor of Hanning.

sentences.zh: 通其貢獻。

translations.literal: His tribute was allowed through.
translations.idiomatic: His tribute missions were accepted at court.

sentences.zh: 韓遂、馬超之亂，關西民奔魯者數万家。

translations.literal: During the turmoil of Han Sui and Ma Chao, several tens of thousands of households from west of the Pass fled to Lu.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Sui and Ma Chao tore Guanxi apart, tens of thousands of families fled to Zhang Lu.

sentences.zh: 時人有地中得玉印者，群下欲尊魯為漢寧王。

translations.literal: Someone at the time obtained a jade seal from the earth; his subordinates wished to honor Lu as king of Hanning.
translations.idiomatic: After a jade seal turned up in the soil, his followers urged elevating him to king of Hanning.

sentences.zh: 魯功曹閻圃諫曰：「漢川之民，戶出十萬，四面險固，財富土沃，上匡天子，則為桓、文，次方竇融，不失富貴。

translations.literal: Lu's merit assessor Yan Pu remonstrated: "The people of the Han river lands furnish one hundred thousand households; on four sides it is precipitous and firm; wealth abounds and the soil is fertile. If above you aid the Son of Heaven, you may become a Huan or Wen; next you may match Dou Rong—not losing riches and honor.
translations.idiomatic: His aide Yan Pu argued: "Hanzhong holds a hundred thousand households behind formidable terrain on fertile, wealthy ground. Aid the emperor and you could rival Duke Huan or Duke Wen; settle for Dou Rong's course and you still keep fortune and rank.

sentences.zh: 今承製署置，勢足斬斷。

translations.literal: Now receiving official appointments by imperial writ, your position is enough to cut decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Your imperial mandate already lets you rule as you see fit.

sentences.zh: 遽稱王號，必為禍先。

translations.literal: To rashly assume a kingly title will surely be the start of calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Leap to a royal title and disaster follows.

sentences.zh: 」魯從之。

translations.literal: " Lu followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Lu took the advice.

sentences.zh: 魯自在漢川垂三十年，聞曹操征之，至陽平，欲舉漢中降。

translations.literal: Lu had himself been in the Han river lands nearly thirty years; hearing that Cao Cao was campaigning against him, when he reached Yangping he wished to surrender Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: After nearly thirty years in Hanzhong, Zhang Lu meant to yield when he heard Cao Cao was coming and reached Yangping.

sentences.zh: 其弟衛不聽，率眾數万，拒關固守。

translations.literal: His younger brother Wei would not listen; he led several tens of thousands, barred the passes, and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Zhang Wei refused, barricaded the passes with tens of thousands, and dug in.

sentences.zh: 操破衛，斬之。

translations.literal: Cao defeated Wei and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao broke Zhang Wei and executed him.

sentences.zh: 魯聞陽平已陷，將稽顙歸降。

translations.literal: Lu heard Yangping had already fallen; he was about to knock forehead to ground and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Yangping had fallen, Zhang Lu prepared to grovel in submission.

sentences.zh: 閻圃說曰：「今以急往，其功為輕，不如且依巴中，然後委質，功必多也。

translations.literal: Yan Pu persuaded him: "Now if you go in haste, your merit will be slight; it is better temporarily to rely on Bazhong, then deliver hostages—your merit will surely be great."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Pu urged him to wait: "Rush to surrender and your credit is thin; withdraw into Bazhong first, then offer allegiance—you will earn far more."

sentences.zh: 」於是乃奔南山。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they fled to the southern mountains.
translations.idiomatic: " They pulled back into the southern hills.

sentences.zh: 左右欲悉焚寶貨倉庫。

translations.literal: Those about him wished to burn all treasures and storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: His staff wanted to torch the treasury and granaries.

sentences.zh: 魯曰：「本欲歸命國家，其意未遂。

translations.literal: Lu said: "Originally I wished to submit my fate to the state; that intent has not yet been fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu said, "I meant all along to submit to the court—only timing stood in the way.

sentences.zh: 今日之走，以避鋒銳，非有惡意。

translations.literal: Today's flight is to avoid sharp edges; there is no evil intent.
translations.idiomatic: This retreat dodges their spearpoints, not malice toward them.

sentences.zh: 」遂封藏而去。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they sealed and stored things and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " So they sealed the stores intact and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 操入南鄭，甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Cao entered Nan Zheng and greatly praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Nan Zheng, Cao Cao applauded the gesture.

sentences.zh: 又以魯本有善意，遣人尉安之。

translations.literal: Moreover because Lu had originally good intentions, he sent men to comfort and reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Zhang Lu's goodwill, he sent envoys to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 魯即與家屬出逆，拜鎮南將軍，封閬中侯，邑萬戶，將還中國，待以客禮。

translations.literal: Lu immediately came out with his household to meet him in submission; he was appointed General Who Guards the South, enfeoffed as marquis of Langzhong with ten thousand households; he was about to return to the central plains and was treated with guest courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu emerged with his family to surrender and received appointment as general who guards the south and marquis of Langzhong with ten thousand households; he was escorted toward the interior as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 封魯五子及閻圃等皆為列侯。

translations.literal: Lu's five sons and Yan Pu and others were all enfeoffed as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: His five sons, Yan Pu, and others were each made full marquises.

sentences.zh: 魯卒，諡曰原侯。

translations.literal: Lu died; his posthumous title was Marquis Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu died and received the posthumous name Marquis Yuan.

sentences.zh: 子富嗣。

translations.literal: His son Fu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhang Fu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 論曰：劉焉睹時方艱，先求後亡之所，庶乎見幾而作。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Liu Yan saw the times were hard and first sought a place from which later he would not perish—perhaps he discerned the signs and acted.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: Liu Yan read the crisis early and secured a bolt-hole—arguably seizing the moment.

sentences.zh: 夫地廣則驕尊之心生，財衍則僭奢之情用，固亦恆人必至之期也。

translations.literal: When territory is broad, a heart of arrogant self-importance arises; when wealth overflows, feelings of presumptuous luxury operate—this is indeed the terminus ordinary men inevitably reach.
translations.idiomatic: Wide lands breed arrogance; overflowing wealth invites extravagance—ordinary men rarely escape that arc.

sentences.zh: 璋能閉隘養力，守案先圖，尚可與歲時推移，而遽輸利器，靜受流斥，所謂羊質虎皮，見豺則恐，籲哉！

translations.literal: Zhang could have closed the passes, nurtured strength, guarded what his ancestors had planned—still he might have shifted with the years; yet hastily he handed over sharp weapons and quietly endured drifting dismissal—what is called sheep nature with tiger skin, seeing a jackal then fearing—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang might have sealed the defiles, husbanded his strength, and held his father's design—buying time—yet he casually surrendered the advantage and meekly accepted banishment: a sheep in a tiger's hide that trembles at jackals—how lamentable!

sentences.zh: 袁術字公路，汝南汝陽人，司空逢之子也。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu, courtesy name Gonglu, was a man of Ruyang in Runan, son of the Minister of Works Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu, styled Gonglu, was a native of Ruyang in Runan and son of Minister of Works Yuan Feng.

sentences.zh: 少以俠氣聞，數與諸​​公子飛鷹走狗，後頗折節。

translations.literal: In youth he was known for knight-errant spirit; often with various young gentlemen he flew hawks and ran dogs; later he somewhat restrained himself.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was famed for swashbuckling bravado—hawking and hunting with other sons of the elite—before moderating his ways.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，累遷至河南尹、虎賁中郎將。

translations.literal: Recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, he was gradually promoted to Governor of the Capital District and General of the Household Gentlemen Tiger Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as filial and incorrupt, he rose through posts to governor of Henan and general of the household gentlemen tiger guards.

sentences.zh: 時，董卓將欲廢立，以術為後將軍。

translations.literal: At the time Dong Zhuo was about to depose one emperor and install another; he appointed Shu General of the Rear.
translations.idiomatic: While Dong Zhuo prepared to replace the emperor on the throne, he named Yuan Shu General of the Rear.

sentences.zh: 術畏卓之禍，出奔南陽。

translations.literal: Shu feared disaster from Zhuo and fled to Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu fled the capital for Nanyang, fearing Dong Zhuo's reach.

sentences.zh: 會長沙太守孫堅殺南陽太守張諮，引兵從術。

translations.literal: At that time Sun Jian, governor of Changsha, killed Zhang Zi, governor of Nanyang, and led troops to join Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian of Changsha had killed Nanyang's governor Zhang Zi and brought his army over to Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 劉表上術為南陽太守，術又表堅領豫州刺史，使率荊、豫之卒，擊破董卓於陽人。

translations.literal: Liu Biao memorialized Shu as governor of Nanyang; Shu in turn memorialized Jian as inspector of Yu Province and ordered him to lead troops from Jing and Yu to defeat Dong Zhuo at Yangren.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao installed Yuan Shu as governor of Nanyang; Yuan Shu then nominated Sun Jian as inspector of Yu and sent him with Jing and Yu troops to crush Dong Zhuo at Yangren.

sentences.zh: 術從兄紹因堅討卓未反，遠，遣其將會稽周昕奪堅豫州。

translations.literal: Shu's cousin Shao, because Jian had not yet returned from campaigning against Zhuo and was far away, sent his general Zhou Xin of Kuaiji to seize Jian's Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: With Sun Jian still far away fighting Dong Zhuo, Yuan Shao sent Zhou Xin of Kuaiji to wrest Yu Province from him.

sentences.zh: 術怒，擊昕走之。

translations.literal: Shu was angry; he attacked Xin and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu struck Zhou Xin and drove him out.

sentences.zh: 紹議欲立劉虞為帝，術好放縱，憚立長君，託以公義不肯同，積此釁隙遂成。

translations.literal: Shao discussed installing Liu Yu as emperor; Shu loved indulgence and feared setting up an elder sovereign; he pleaded public righteousness and refused to agree—bad blood piled up from this.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao wanted to place Liu Yu on the throne; Yuan Shu, loose-living and unwilling to serve an older lord, hid behind empty rhetoric and refused—their feud hardened.

sentences.zh: 乃各外交黨援，以相圖謀，術結公孫瓚，而紹連劉表。

translations.literal: Thereupon each cultivated outside allies to plot against the other: Shu allied with Gongsun Zan, while Shao linked with Liu Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Each man then courted foreign backers: Yuan Shu joined Gongsun Zan; Yuan Shao leaned on Liu Biao.

sentences.zh: 豪桀多附於紹，術怒曰：「群豎不吾從，而從吾家奴乎！

translations.literal: Many heroes attached to Shao; Shu angrily said: "These petty fellows do not follow me—they follow my family's slave!"
translations.idiomatic: Most warlords favored Yuan Shao, and Yuan Shu fumed, "So these nobodies follow my household slave instead of me!"

sentences.zh: 」又與公孫瓚書，雲紹非袁氏子，紹聞大怒。

translations.literal: " He also wrote Gongsun Zan that Shao was not a true son of the Yuan clan; Shao heard and was furious.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Gongsun Zan claiming Yuan Shao was no true Yuan—a lie that enraged Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 初平三年，術遣孫堅擊劉表於襄陽，堅戰死。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chuping, Shu sent Sun Jian to attack Liu Biao at Xiangyang; Jian died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In 192 Yuan Shu sent Sun Jian against Liu Biao at Xiangyang; Sun Jian fell in action.

sentences.zh: 公孫瓚使劉備與術合謀共逼紹，紹與曹操會擊，皆破之。

translations.literal: Gongsun Zan had Liu Bei join Shu in pressuring Shao; Shao and Cao Cao jointly attacked and defeated them all.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zan paired Liu Bei with Yuan Shu to squeeze Yuan Shao; Yuan Shao and Cao Cao joined forces and broke them.

sentences.zh: 四年，術引軍入陳留，屯封丘。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Shu led troops into Chenliu and encamped at Fengqiu.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Yuan Shu marched into Chenliu and camped at Fengqiu.

sentences.zh: 黑山餘賊及匈奴於扶羅等佐術，與曹操戰於匡亭，大敗。

translations.literal: Black Mountain remnant bandits and the Xiongnu chieftain Yufu Luo assisted Shu; they fought Cao Cao at Kuangting and suffered a crushing defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel remnants from Black Mountain and the Xiongnu leader Yufu Luo fought beside Yuan Shu at Kuangting—and Cao Cao shattered them.

sentences.zh: 術退保雍丘，又將其餘眾奔九江，殺楊州刺史陳溫而自領之，又兼稱徐州伯。

translations.literal: Shu fell back to Yongqiu, then led his survivors to Jiujiang, killed Inspector Chen Wen of Yang Province and took his place, and also styled himself lord of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu withdrew to Yongqiu, then bolted to Jiujiang, murdered Yang Province's inspector Chen Wen, seized his office, and dubbed himself lord of Xu.

sentences.zh: 李傕入長安，欲結術為援，乃授以左將軍，假節，封陽翟侯。

translations.literal: When Li Jue entered Chang'an and wished to win Shu as an ally, he appointed him General of the Left, granted credentials, and enfeoffed him as marquis of Yangdi.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Jue took Chang'an he courted Yuan Shu, naming him General of the Left with insignia and the marquisate of Yangdi.

sentences.zh: 初，術在南陽，戶口尚數十百萬，而不修法度，以抄掠為資，奢恣無猒，百姓患之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shu was in Nanyang, registered households still numbered in the millions, yet he did not establish laws; he lived by plunder, indulged without satiety, and the people suffered him.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanyang Yuan Shu ruled millions but ignored law, funded himself by looting, and lived without restraint while the populace groaned.

sentences.zh: 又少見讖書，言「代漢者當塗高」，自云名字應之。

translations.literal: He also occasionally read prophetic texts saying "He who replaces Han will be from Dangtu Gao"; he claimed his name answered it.
translations.idiomatic: He latched onto the prophecy that "the successor to Han is at Dangtu Gao" and insisted his own name matched it.

sentences.zh: 又以袁氏出陳為舜後，以黃代赤，德運之次，遂有僭逆之謀。

translations.literal: He also held that the Yuan clan sprang from Chen as descendants of Shun; yellow would replace red by the cycle of virtue—thereupon he harbored treasonous designs.
translations.idiomatic: He argued the Yuans, via Chen, descended from Shun, so the yellow virtue should follow the red—and began plotting usurpation.

sentences.zh: 又聞孫堅得傳國璽，遂拘堅妻奪之。

translations.literal: He further heard that Sun Jian had obtained the imperial seal; thereupon he detained Jian's wife and seized it.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Sun Jian held the jade seal, he imprisoned Sun Jian's wife and took it by force.

sentences.zh: 興平二年冬，天子播越，敗於曹陽。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Xingping, the Son of Heaven was driven forth and defeated at Caoyang.
translations.idiomatic: That winter of 195 the emperor fled in disorder and was routed at Caoyang.

sentences.zh: 術大會群下，因謂曰：「今海內鼎沸，劉氏微弱。

translations.literal: Shu convened his officers and said to them: "Now within the seas all boils; the Liu house is feeble.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu assembled his court and declared, "The realm is in turmoil and the Han house weak.

sentences.zh: 吾家四世公輔，百姓所歸，欲應天順民，於諸君何如？

translations.literal: Our house for four generations has held the highest offices; the people turn to us. I wish to answer Heaven and follow the people—what say you, gentlemen?"
translations.idiomatic: For four generations my clan has served as chief ministers; the people look to us. I mean to answer Heaven and win the people—what do you say?"

sentences.zh: 」眾莫敢對。

translations.literal: " None dared reply.
translations.idiomatic: No one answered.

sentences.zh: 主簿閻象進曰：「昔周自后稷至於文王，積德累功，參分天下，猶服事殷。

translations.literal: Registrar Yan Xiang stepped forward: "Of old Zhou from Hou Ji down to King Wen piled up virtue and merit and held a third of the realm, yet still served Yin."
translations.idiomatic: Registrar Yan Xiang objected: "From Hou Ji to King Wen the Zhou piled merit for generations and held only a third of the realm, yet still served the Shang."

sentences.zh: 明公雖奕世克昌，孰若有周之盛？

translations.literal: Though my lord's line flourishes age after age, who compares with Zhou at its height?
translations.idiomatic: Your house may thrive for generations, but has it Zhou's stature?"

sentences.zh: 漢室雖微，未至殷紂之敝也。

translations.literal: The Han house, though slight, has not reached the ruin of Yin Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: Han may be declining, but it is no ruined Shang under Zhou Xin."

sentences.zh: 」術嘿然，使召張範。

translations.literal: " Shu fell silent and ordered Zhang Fan summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu fell silent and sent for Zhang Fan.

sentences.zh: 範辭疾，遣弟承往應之。

translations.literal: Fan pleaded illness and sent his younger brother Cheng to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fan pleaded illness and deputized his brother Zhang Cheng.

sentences.zh: 術問曰「昔周室陵遲，則有桓、文之霸；

translations.literal: Shu asked: "When the Zhou house declined, there were the hegemons Huan and Wen;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu asked, "When Zhou waned, Huan and Wen rose as hegemons;

sentences.zh: 秦失其政，漢接而用之。

translations.literal: Qin lost good rule and Han picked it up.
translations.idiomatic: Qin forfeited the mandate and Han succeeded.

sentences.zh: 今孤以土地之廣，士人之眾，欲徼福於齊桓，擬跡於高祖，可乎？

translations.literal: Now I, with the breadth of my lands and host of scholars, wish to seek fortune like Duke Huan of Qi and tread in the tracks of the Gaozu—may I?"
translations.idiomatic: Now I command broad territory and many men—may I win fortune like Duke Huan or walk in Gaozu's steps?"

sentences.zh: 」承對曰：「在德不在眾。

translations.literal: " Cheng replied: "Power lies in virtue, not numbers."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cheng answered, "Strength rests in virtue, not head count."

sentences.zh: 苟能用德以同天下之欲，雖云匹夫，霸王可也。

translations.literal: If you can use virtue to align with the desires of the realm, though you be but a common man, you may become a hegemon king.
translations.idiomatic: Align the empire through virtue and even a commoner can rise as hegemon.

sentences.zh: 若陵僭無度，乾時而動，眾之所棄，誰能興之！

translations.literal: If you presumptuously overstep bounds and move against the hour, abandoned by the multitude—who can raise you!"
translations.idiomatic: Usurp without measure and move against the times, and when men abandon you, who will lift you up?"

sentences.zh: 」術不說。

translations.literal: " Shu was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu took offense.

sentences.zh: 自孫堅死，子策复領其部曲，術遣擊楊州刺史劉繇，破之，策因據江東。

translations.literal: After Sun Jian died, his son Ce again led his lieutenants; Shu dispatched him to attack Inspector Liu Yao of Yang Province, defeated him, and Ce thereupon occupied Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Jian's death Sun Ce led his father's troops at Yuan Shu's bidding, crushed Liu Yao in Yang Province, and seized south of the Long River.

sentences.zh: 策聞術將欲僭號，與書諫曰：

translations.literal: Ce heard Shu was about to assume an imperial title and wrote remonstrating:
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce learned Yuan Shu would declare himself emperor, he wrote to dissuade him:

sentences.zh: 董卓無道，陵虐王室，禍加太后，暴及弘農，天子播越，宮廟焚毀，是以豪桀發憤，沛然俱起。

translations.literal: " Dong Zhuo was lawless; he abused the royal house, calamity reached the empress dowager, violence extended to Hongnong; the Son of Heaven was driven forth, palace temples burned—therefore heroes rose in wrath together."
translations.idiomatic: "Dong Zhuo trampled the court, harmed the dowager and the Prince of Hongnong, drove out the emperor, and burned the shrines—so loyal men rose as one."

sentences.zh: 元惡既斃，幼主東顧，乃使王人奉命，宣明朝恩，偃武修文，與之更始。

translations.literal: Once the chief villain was dead, the young sovereign looked east; envoys carried commands, proclaiming court grace, laying down arms and cultivating letters, granting all a fresh start.
translations.idiomatic: With Dong Zhuo gone the boy emperor turned east; imperial messengers announced renewal of Han grace and called for peace.

sentences.zh: 然而河北異謀於黑山，曹操毒被於東徐，劉表僭亂於南荊，公孫叛逆於朔北，正禮阻兵，玄德爭盟，是以未獲從命，橐弓戢戈。

translations.literal: Yet north of the Yellow River Black Mountain plotted differently; Cao Cao's poison spread over eastern Xu; Liu Biao usurped order in southern Jing; Gongsun rebelled on the northern frontier; Liu Yao (courtesy Zhengli) blocked the road with arms; Xuande contested alliances—therefore orders could not yet be obeyed and bows stayed unslung.
translations.idiomatic: Yet troubles multiplied—Black Mountain in Hebei, Cao Cao scourging Xu, Liu Biao unsettling southern Jing, Gongsun Zan in the far north, Liu Yao holding his army in check, Liu Bei maneuvering for advantage—so we could not yet sheath swords.

sentences.zh: 當謂使君與國同規，而捨是弗卹，完然有自取之志，懼非海內企望之意也。

translations.literal: We supposed you shared the state's standard, yet you disregard this and show no pity, calmly harboring designs to seize power yourself—I fear this is not what the realm expects.
translations.idiomatic: We thought you stood with the dynasty; instead you nurse private ambition without pity—that cannot be what the empire hopes for.

sentences.zh: 成湯討桀，稱：有夏多罪」；

translations.literal: Tang attacking Jie declared: "Xia's crimes are many";
translations.idiomatic: When Tang attacked Jie he cited Xia's crimes;

sentences.zh: 武王討紂，曰「殷有重罰」。

translations.literal: Wu attacking Zhou said "Yin bears heavy punishment."
translations.idiomatic: When Wu marched on Zhou he cited Shang's guilt.

sentences.zh: 此二王者，雖有聖德，假使時無失道之過，無由逼而取也。

translations.literal: Those two kings, though possessed of sagely virtue, had there been no fault of the hour to seize, had no cause to force and take.
translations.idiomatic: Even those sage kings needed a wicked court before they could seize power.

sentences.zh: 今主上非有惡於天下，徒以幼小脅於強臣，異於湯、武之時也。

translations.literal: Now our sovereign has done no evil to the realm; he is merely young and pressed by strong ministers—this differs from Tang and Wu's hour.
translations.idiomatic: Today's emperor has wronged no one; he is young and trapped by warlords—not Shang's terminal decay.

sentences.zh: 又聞幼主明智聰敏，有夙成之德，天下雖未被其恩，咸歸心焉。

translations.literal: I further hear the young lord is wise and keen, endowed with precocious virtue; though the realm has not yet felt his kindness, all hearts turn to him.
translations.idiomatic: They say the boy ruler is wise beyond his years; though his grace has not spread, the people already incline to him.

sentences.zh: 若輔而興之，則旦、奭之美，率土所望也。

translations.literal: If you aid and raise him, you may rival Dan and Shi—the whole land desires it.
translations.idiomatic: Aid him as the Duke of Zhou aided King Cheng and the realm will praise you.

sentences.zh: 使君五世相承，為漢宰輔，榮寵之盛，莫與為比，宜效忠守節，以報王室。

translations.literal: Your house for five generations has served Han as chief ministers; glory matches none—you should show loyalty and integrity to repay the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations of Yuans have served as Han's chief ministers; none match your honor—you owe fealty, not ambition.

sentences.zh: 時人多惑圖緯之言，妄牽非類之文，苟以悅主為美，不顧成敗之計，古今所慎，可不熟慮！

translations.literal: Men of the age are much misled by charts and weft texts, rashly dragging in irrelevant passages, pleasing their lord for praise without heed to success or failure—what ages past have dreaded; can you not weigh it carefully!
translations.idiomatic: Many chase omens and twist prophecies to flatter princes without weighing ruin—think hard before you leap!

sentences.zh: 忠言逆耳，駁議致憎，苟有益於尊明，無所敢辭。

translations.literal: Loyal words grate the ear; dissent breeds hatred—yet if it profits your honor, I dare not shrink.
translations.idiomatic: Truth may sting and debates annoy, but if they serve you I will speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 術不納，策遂絕之。

translations.literal: Shu did not accept; Ce thereupon broke with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu ignored him; Sun Ce cut ties.

sentences.zh: 建安二年，因河內張炯符命，遂果僭號，自稱「仲家」。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jian'an, relying on Zhang Jiong of Henei's talismanic mandate, he then assumed a usurped title and styled himself "Zhongjia."
translations.idiomatic: In 197, citing Zhang Jiong of Henei's forged prophecy, Yuan Shu declared himself emperor under the reign title "Zhongjia."

sentences.zh: 以九江太守為淮南尹，置公卿百官，郊祀天地。

translations.literal: He made the governor of Jiujiang grand steward of Huainan, installed dukes and ministers and myriad offices, and sacrificed to Heaven and Earth in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: He renamed Jiujiang's governor grand steward of Huainan, erected a full court, and performed suburban sacrifices as emperor.

sentences.zh: 乃遣使以竊號告呂布，並為子娉布女。

translations.literal: He then sent envoys to inform Lü Bu of his stolen title and also arranged for his son to marry Bu's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: He notified Lü Bu of his imperial claim and betrothed his son to Lü Bu's daughter.

sentences.zh: 布執術使送許。

translations.literal: Bu seized Shu's envoys and sent them to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu arrested his messengers and forwarded them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 術大怒，遣其將張勛、橋蕤攻布，大敗而還。

translations.literal: Shu was greatly angry; he sent his generals Zhang Xun and Qiao Rui to attack Bu and was badly defeated returning.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu struck back with Zhang Xun and Qiao Rui—and suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 術又率兵擊陳國，誘殺其王寵及相駱俊，曹操乃自征之。

translations.literal: Shu again led troops to strike Chen principality, enticed and killed its prince Liu Chong and chancellor Luo Jun—thereupon Cao Cao personally campaigned against him.
translations.idiomatic: He invaded Chen, murdered Prince Liu Chong and Chancellor Luo Jun by treachery, and drew Cao Cao's personal expedition.

sentences.zh: 術聞大駭，即走度淮，留張勛、橋蕤於蘄陽，以拒操。

translations.literal: Shu heard and was terrified; he immediately fled across the Huai, leaving Zhang Xun and Qiao Rui at Qiyang to resist Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Panic-stricken, Yuan Shu fled south of the Huai, leaving Zhang Xun and Qiao Rui at Qiyang to hold Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 操擊破斬蕤，而勳退走。

translations.literal: Cao attacked, defeated, and beheaded Rui, while Xun fled.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao smashed them, killed Qiao Rui, and Zhang Xun ran.

sentences.zh: 術兵弱，大將死，眾情離叛，加天旱歲荒，士民凍餒，江、淮間相食殆盡。

translations.literal: Shu's troops were weak, great generals dead, hearts rebelled in separation; moreover drought desolated the year—gentlemen and commoners froze and starved; between the Yangzi and Huai men ate one another nearly to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu's army was spent, his champions gone, his men deserting; drought and famine left officials and peasants starving until the Jiang-Huai corridor cannibalized itself.

sentences.zh: 時，舒仲應為術沛相，術以米十萬斛與為軍糧，仲應悉散以給饑民。

translations.literal: At that time Shu Zhongying was Yuan Shu's chancellor of Pei; Shu gave him one hundred thousand hu of rice as army grain, but Zhongying distributed it all to the starving people.
translations.idiomatic: Pei's chancellor Shu Zhongying took the hundred thousand hu Yuan Shu allotted for the army and fed every grain to the starving.

sentences.zh: 術聞怒，陳兵將斬之。

translations.literal: Shu heard and was angry; he drew up troops intending to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu raged and prepared to execute him.

sentences.zh: 仲應曰：「知當必死，故為之耳。

translations.literal: Zhongying said: "I knew I must die—therefore I did it.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Zhongying replied, "I knew it meant death—that is why I did it.

sentences.zh: 寧可以一人之命，救百姓於塗炭。

translations.literal: Better one man's life may rescue the hundred surnames from mud and charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: One life is a fair trade to pull the people from ruin.

sentences.zh: 」術下馬牽之曰：「仲應，足下獨欲享天下重名，不與吾共之邪？」

translations.literal: " Shu dismounted and took his hand: "Zhongying—do you alone wish to enjoy the realm's great name and not share it with me?"
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Shu dismounted and seized his arm: "You only want the fame for yourself and will not share it with me?"

sentences.zh: 術雖矜名尚奇，而天性驕肆，尊己陵物。

translations.literal: Though Shu prized renown and admired the extraordinary, his nature was arrogant and unrestrained, honoring himself and slighting others.
translations.idiomatic: For all his posturing, Yuan Shu was arrogant by nature—vaunting himself and trampling others.

sentences.zh: 及竊偽號，淫侈滋甚，媵禦數百，無不兼羅紈，厭梁肉，自下飢困，莫之簡卹。

translations.literal: When he stole a false title, debauchery swelled yet more: hundreds of concubines and attendants, none without silk gauze, surfeited with fine grain and meat; below, the hungry languished—none received relief.
translations.idiomatic: Once crowned, his excess grew: hundreds of women in gauze and satin while soldiers starved—he never spared them a thought.

sentences.zh: 於是資實空盡，不能自立。

translations.literal: Thereupon his resources emptied utterly and he could not stand on his own.
translations.idiomatic: His treasury ran dry and his regime collapsed.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，乃燒宮室，奔其部曲陳簡、雷薄於灊山。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year he burned the palace halls and fled to his lieutenants Chen Jian and Lei Bo in Mount Qian.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of 199 he torched his palace and fled to Chen Jian and Lei Bo in the Qian Mountains.

sentences.zh: 復為簡等所拒，遂大困窮，士卒散走。

translations.literal: Again rejected by Jian and the others, he fell into extreme distress; soldiers scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: They shut him out; his men melted away.

sentences.zh: 憂懣不知所為，遂歸帝號於紹，曰：「祿去漢室久矣，天下提挈，政在家門。

translations.literal: Anguished, knowing nothing to do, he returned the imperial title to Shao, saying: "Fortune left the house of Han long ago; the realm is wrested about—government sits in great families.
translations.idiomatic: Broken and desperate, he surrendered his bogus throne to Yuan Shao: "Han's mandate is long gone; warlords carve up the realm."

sentences.zh: 豪雄角逐，分割疆宇。

translations.literal: Heroes contend and carve border lands.
translations.idiomatic: It is the Warring States again—only the strong swallow the weak.

sentences.zh: 此與周末七國無異，唯強者兼之耳。

translations.literal: This differs in nothing from the seven states at Zhou's end—only the mighty annex others.
translations.idiomatic: No different from the last days of Zhou—the ruthless annex the rest.

sentences.zh: 袁氏受命當王，符瑞炳然。

translations.literal: The Yuan house received Heaven's mandate to rule as king—omens blaze bright.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven marks the Yuans for kingship—the signs are clear.

sentences.zh: 今君擁有四州，人戶百萬，以強則莫與爭大，以位則無所比高。

translations.literal: Now you hold four provinces and a million households; in strength none rivals your greatness; in rank none compares higher.
translations.idiomatic: You command four provinces and a million souls—none match your might or standing.

sentences.zh: 曹操雖欲扶衰獎微，安能續絕運，起已滅乎！

translations.literal: Though Cao Cao wishes to shore up the fading and praise the slight, how can he mend a severed mandate or revive what is extinct!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao cannot prop up a dead dynasty or breathe life into ashes!

sentences.zh: 謹歸大命，君其興之。

translations.literal: I respectfully return the great mandate—rise, my lord.
translations.idiomatic: I hand you the seal—take it and rise.

sentences.zh: 」紹陰然其計。

translations.literal: " Shao secretly approved the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao quietly welcomed the offer.

sentences.zh: 術因欲北至青州從袁譚，曹操使劉備徼之，不得過，复走還壽春。

translations.literal: Shu then wished to go north to Qing Province to join Yuan Tan; Cao Cao had Liu Bei intercept him—unable to pass, he fled back to Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to reach Yuan Tan in Qingzhou; Liu Bei blocked him for Cao Cao, so he slunk back to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 六月，至江亭。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he reached Jiang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: That sixth month he dragged himself to Jiang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 坐簣床而歎曰：「袁術乃至是乎！

translations.literal: Sitting on a rush bed he sighed: "Has Yuan Shu truly come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Collapsed on a pallet of straw he groaned, "So this is how far Yuan Shu has fallen!

sentences.zh: 」因憤慨結病，歐血死。

translations.literal: " Thereupon indignation knotted into illness; he vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: " Shame and rage broke him; he coughed blood and died.

sentences.zh: 妻子依故吏廬江太守劉勛。

translations.literal: His wife and children relied on former clerk Liu Xun, governor of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: His family took shelter with Liu Xun of Lujiang, an old retainer.

sentences.zh: 孫策破勳，復見收視，術女入孫權宮，子曜仕吳為郎中。

translations.literal: Sun Ce defeated Xun; they were again taken in charge; Shu's daughter entered Sun Quan's palace; his son Yao served Wu as a gentleman of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce crushed Liu Xun and absorbed the household—Yuan Shu's daughter entered Sun Quan's harem and his son Yuan Yao served Wu as a court gentleman.

sentences.zh: 論曰：「天命符驗，可得而見，未可得而言也。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: "Heaven's mandate and talismanic verification may be seen yet cannot be spoken.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: "Portents may be glimpsed yet resist plain speech.

sentences.zh: 然大致受大福者，歸於信順乎！

translations.literal: Yet those who receive great blessing mostly come down to trusting obedience!
translations.idiomatic: Still, lasting fortune favors good faith.

sentences.zh: 夫事不以順，雖強力廣謀，不能得也。

translations.literal: When affairs do not accord with submission, though one apply force and broad schemes, one cannot obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Work against Heaven and no clever plot avails.

sentences.zh: 謀不可得之事，日失忠信，變詐妄生矣。

translations.literal: Scheming for what cannot be obtained, daily losing loyalty and trust, shifts and frauds arise.
translations.idiomatic: Chasing impossible thrones erodes trust and breeds deceit.

sentences.zh: 況復苟肆行之，其以欺天乎！

translations.literal: Moreover if one rashly indulges in acting thus, does one thereby deceive Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Persist in fraud and you mock Heaven itself!

sentences.zh: 雖假符僭稱，歸將安所容哉！

translations.literal: Though one borrow talismans and usurp titles—where shall one finally find shelter!
translations.idiomatic: Forged omens buy no refuge—where will you hide?"

sentences.zh: 呂布字奉先，五原九原人也。

translations.literal: Lü Bu, courtesy name Fengxian, was a man of Jiuyuan in Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu, styled Fengxian, came from Jiuyuan in Wuyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 以弓馬驍武給并州。

translations.literal: Because of skill at bow and horse and fierce bravery he was assigned to Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned archer and horseman, he entered service in Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 刺史丁原為騎都尉，原屯河內，以布為主簿，甚見親待。

translations.literal: Inspector Ding Yuan was colonel of the carriage and cavalry; Yuan encamped in Henei and appointed Bu chief clerk, treating him with great intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Ding Yuan, colonel of carriage and cavalry, camped at Henei and made Lü Bu his chief clerk, favoring him warmly.

sentences.zh: 靈帝崩，原受何進召，將兵詣洛陽，為執金吾。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ling died, Yuan received He Jin's summons, led troops to Luoyang, and became Bearer of the Gilded Mace.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ling's death Ding Yuan answered He Jin's call, marched on Luoyang, and became Bearer of the Gilded Mace.

sentences.zh: 會進敗，董卓誘布殺原而併其兵。

translations.literal: When Jin was defeated, Dong Zhuo enticed Bu to kill Yuan and annex his troops.
translations.idiomatic: When He Jin fell, Dong Zhuo bribed Lü Bu into killing Ding Yuan and seizing his army.

sentences.zh: 卓以布為騎都尉，誓為父子，甚愛信之。

translations.literal: Zhuo appointed Bu colonel of the carriage and cavalry; they swore father-son ties and Zhuo greatly loved and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo named him colonel of carriage and cavalry; they swore a foster tie and Dong Zhuo doted on him.

sentences.zh: 稍遷至中郎將，封都亭侯。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to general of the household and enfeoffed as marquis of Metropolitan Village.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to general of the household and marquis of Metropolitan Village.

sentences.zh: 卓自知凶恣，每懷猜畏，行止常以布自衛。

translations.literal: Zhuo knew himself cruel and headstrong; always harboring suspicion and fear, in movement and rest he constantly used Bu to guard himself.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing his own brutality, Dong Zhuo stayed wary and kept Lü Bu as bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 嘗小失卓意，卓拔手戟擲之。

translations.literal: Once he slightly missed Zhuo's intention; Zhuo drew the hand halberd and threw it at him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lü Bu crossed him; Dong Zhuo hurled a halberd at his head.

sentences.zh: 布拳捷得免，而改容顧謝，卓意亦解。

translations.literal: Bu blocked with his fists and was spared; he changed expression and apologized, and Zhuo's anger also eased.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu dodged the blow and apologized; Dong Zhuo's rage cooled.

sentences.zh: 布由是陰怨於卓。

translations.literal: Bu therefore secretly harbored resentment toward Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Lü Bu nursed a secret grudge against Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 卓又使布守中閤，而私與傅婢情通，益不自安。

translations.literal: Zhuo again had Bu guard the inner chambers; he privately carried on with a chambermaid—Bu grew ever less secure.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo assigned him to guard the inner palace while sleeping with a maid—Lü Bu grew anxious.

sentences.zh: 因往見司徒王允，自陳卓幾見殺之狀。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went to see Minister of Education Wang Yun and laid out how Zhuo had nearly killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He sought Wang Yun and described how Dong Zhuo had nearly murdered him.

sentences.zh: 時允與尚書僕射士孫瑞密謀誅卓，因以告布，使為內應。

translations.literal: At that time Yun with Imperial Secretariat Supervisor Sun Rui secretly plotted to kill Zhuo; he therefore informed Bu and made him inner collaborator.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun was already plotting Dong Zhuo's death with Sun Rui; he enlisted Lü Bu as insider.

sentences.zh: 布曰：「如父子何？

translations.literal: Bu said: "What of our father-son bond?"
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu asked, "But we swore as father and son."

sentences.zh: 」曰：「君自姓呂，本非骨肉。

translations.literal: " They said: "You bear the surname Lü—you are not bone and flesh."
translations.idiomatic: "You are a Lü by blood—not truly kin."

sentences.zh: 今憂死不暇，何謂父子？

translations.literal: Now you fret death without respite—what father-son sentiment remains?
translations.idiomatic: "You fear for your life—what bond is left?"

sentences.zh: 擲戟之時，豈有父子情也？

translations.literal: When he hurled the halberd, was there father-son feeling?
translations.idiomatic: "Did he show fatherly mercy when he threw that halberd?"

sentences.zh: 」布遂許之，乃於門刺殺卓，事已見《卓傳》。

translations.literal: " Bu consented; he therefore assassinated Zhuo at the gate—the affair is recorded in Zhuo's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu agreed and stabbed Dong Zhuo at the gate, as told in Dong Zhuo's memoir.

sentences.zh: 允以布為奮威將軍，假節，儀同三司，封溫侯。

translations.literal: Yun appointed Bu General Who Displays Might, granted credentials, ceremonial parity with the Three Dukes, and enfeoffed him marquis of Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun named him General Who Displays Might with insignia and Three Dukes' honors, marquis of Wen.

sentences.zh: 允既不赦涼州人，由是卓將李傕等遂相結，還攻長安。

translations.literal: Because Yun would not pardon men from Liangzhou, Zhuo's generals Li Jue and others banded together and returned to attack Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun refused amnesty for Liangzhou troops, so Li Jue and Dong Zhuo's old guard marched back on Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 布與傕戰，敗，乃將數百騎，以卓頭系馬鞍，走出武關，奔南陽。

translations.literal: Bu fought Jue and was defeated; he led several hundred horse, tied Zhuo's head to his saddle, fled through Wu Pass to Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Beaten by Li Jue, Lü Bu fled with a few hundred riders, Dong Zhuo's head lashed to his saddle, through Wu Pass toward Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 袁術待之甚厚。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu received him lavishly.

sentences.zh: 布自恃殺卓，有德袁氏，遂恣兵抄掠。

translations.literal: Bu trusted that killing Zhuo had earned him merit with the Yuan clan; thereupon he let his troops plunder at will.
translations.idiomatic: Sure his deed had earned the Yuans' gratitude, he let his men loot.

sentences.zh: 術患之。

translations.literal: Shu was troubled by it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu soon wearied of him.

sentences.zh: 布不安，复去從張楊於河內。

translations.literal: Bu was uneasy and again left to join Zhang Yang in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy, Lü Bu crossed to Zhang Yang in Henei.

sentences.zh: 時李傕等購募求布急，楊下諸將皆欲圖之。

translations.literal: At that time Li Jue and others urgently offered reward for Bu; Yang's subordinate generals all wished to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue's price on his head tempted every officer under Zhang Yang.

sentences.zh: 布懼，謂楊曰：「與卿州里，今見殺，其功未必多。

translations.literal: Bu feared; he said to Yang: "We are countrymen—if you kill me now, the reward may not be great.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu pleaded, "We hail from the same commandery; killing me earns little."

sentences.zh: 不如生賣布，可大得傕等爵寵。

translations.literal: Better sell Bu alive—you may win great ennoblement from Jue and company.
translations.idiomatic: "Deliver me alive and Li Jue will pay far better."

sentences.zh: 」楊以為然。

translations.literal: " Yang deemed it so.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yang agreed.

sentences.zh: 有頃，布得走投袁紹，紹與布擊張燕于常山。

translations.literal: Before long Bu won chance to flee to Yuan Shao; Shao with Bu attacked Zhang Yan in Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: He slipped away to Yuan Shao and joined him against Zhang Yan of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 燕精兵萬餘，騎數千匹。

translations.literal: Yan had over ten thousand crack troops and several thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan commanded ten thousand veterans and thousands of mounts.

sentences.zh: 布常禦良馬，號曰赤菟，能馳城飛塹，與其健將成廉、魏越等數十騎馳突燕陣，一日或至三四，皆斬首而出。

translations.literal: Bu habitually rode a fine horse called Red Hare, able to gallop walls and leap moats; with his stalwart generals Cheng Lian, Wei Yue, and several tens of riders he charged Yan's formation three or four times a day, each time beheading and breaking out.
translations.idiomatic: On Red Hare he vaulted walls and ditches, charging Zhang Yan's lines three or four times a day at the head of Cheng Lian, Wei Yue, and a handful of riders—each pass leaving heads behind.

sentences.zh: 連戰十餘日，遂破燕軍。

translations.literal: They fought continuously over ten days and finally broke Yan's army.
translations.idiomatic: After ten days of fighting they shattered Zhang Yan.

sentences.zh: 布既恃其功，更請兵於紹，紹不許，而將士多暴橫，紹患之。

translations.literal: Bu, trusting his merit, further requested troops from Shao; Shao did not permit it, while his officers behaved violently—Shao was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Flush with victory he demanded more troops; Yuan Shao refused while Lü Bu's men terrorized the countryside.

sentences.zh: 布不自安，因求還洛陽。

translations.literal: Bu was not secure within himself and requested return to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, he asked leave to return west.

sentences.zh: 紹聽之，承製使領司隸校尉，遣壯士送布而陰使殺之。

translations.literal: Shao listened; acting by imperial writ he made him Colonel Director of Retainers and sent braves to escort Bu while secretly ordering them to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao named him colonel director of retainers and sent an escort meant to murder him en route.

sentences.zh: 布疑其圖己，乃使人鼓箏於帳中，潛自遁出。

translations.literal: Bu suspected they plotted against him; he had someone play the zheng inside the tent while he slipped away unseen.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the trap, he staged a zheng performance in his tent and stole away.

sentences.zh: 夜中兵起，而布已亡。

translations.literal: In the night soldiers rose—but Bu had already fled.
translations.idiomatic: That night the assassins struck an empty bed.

sentences.zh: 紹聞，懼為患，募遣追之，皆莫敢逼，遂歸張楊。

translations.literal: Shao heard and feared he would become a scourge; he hired pursuers—none dared close—and Bu returned to Zhang Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao put hunters on his trail, but none would face him; Lü Bu rejoined Zhang Yang.

sentences.zh: 道經陳留，太守張邈遣使迎之，相待甚厚，臨別把臂言誓。

translations.literal: Passing through Chenliu, Governor Zhang Miao sent envoys to welcome him, treated him generously, and at parting clasped arms and swore oaths.
translations.idiomatic: Chenliu's Zhang Miao met him with honors and swore friendship at farewell.

sentences.zh: 曹操聞而引軍擊布，累戰，相持百餘日。

translations.literal: Cao Cao heard and led troops to strike Bu; they fought repeatedly and stalemate lasted over a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao marched against him and fought to a hundred-day standoff.

sentences.zh: 是時，旱、蝗，少穀，百姓相食，布移屯山陽。

translations.literal: At that time drought and locusts left little grain; commoners ate one another; Bu shifted camp to Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Drought and locusts emptied the granaries and turned peasants to cannibalism; Lü Bu withdrew toward Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 二年間，操复盡收諸城，破布於鉅野，布東奔劉備。

translations.literal: Within two years Cao again recovered all the cities, defeated Bu at Juye, and Bu fled east to Liu Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Within two years Cao Cao retook the towns, crushed him at Juye, and drove him to Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 邈詣袁術求救，留超將家屬屯雍丘。

translations.literal: Miao went to Yuan Shu begging rescue; he left Chao to guard family dependents encamped at Yongqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Miao raced to Yuan Shu for aid while Zhang Chao guarded his kin at Yongqiu.

sentences.zh: 操圍超數月，屠之，滅其三族。

translations.literal: Cao besieged Chao several months, slaughtered the city, and extinguished three clans.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao invested Yongqiu for months, sacked it, and extirpated Zhang Chao's kin.

sentences.zh: 邈未至壽春，為其兵所害。

translations.literal: Before Miao reached Shouchun, his own troops killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Miao never reached Shouchun—his soldiers cut him down.

sentences.zh: 時，劉備領徐州，居下邳，與袁術相拒於淮上。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Bei held Xu Province, dwelt at Xiapi, and confronted Yuan Shu along the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei governed Xu from Xiapi, facing Yuan Shu on the Huai.

sentences.zh: 術欲引布擊備，乃與布書曰：「術舉兵詣闕，未能屠裂董卓。

translations.literal: Shu wished to draw Bu to strike Bei; he therefore wrote Bu: "Shu raised troops toward the capital yet could not tear Dong Zhuo apart.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu wrote Lü Bu: "I marched on the capital but failed to butcher Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 將軍誅卓，為術報恥，功一也。

translations.literal: The general executed Zhuo, avenging Shu's shame—the first merit.
translations.idiomatic: You executed Dong Zhuo and wiped away my shame—that is your first debt I owe."

sentences.zh: 昔金元休南至封丘，為曹操所敗。

translations.literal: Formerly Jin Yuanxiu went south to Fengqiu and was defeated by Cao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: "When Jin Yuanxiu fled to Fengqiu, Cao Cao crushed him."

sentences.zh: 將軍伐之，令術復明目於遐邇，功二也。

translations.literal: The general attacked him, letting Shu recover face near and far—the second merit.
translations.idiomatic: You crushed him and restored my name—that is the second."

sentences.zh: 術生年以來，不聞天下有劉備，備乃舉兵與術對戰。

translations.literal: All my life I had not heard of Liu Bei in the realm—Bei thereupon raised troops to battle Shu.
translations.idiomatic: "I never heard of Liu Bei until he took arms against me."

sentences.zh: 憑將軍威靈，得以破備，功三也。

translations.literal: Relying on the general's awesome might I could defeat Bei—the third merit.
translations.idiomatic: By your might I broke him—that is the third."

sentences.zh: 將軍有三大功在術，術雖不敏，奉以死生。

translations.literal: The general holds three great merits toward Shu; though Shu is dull, I pledge life and death.
translations.idiomatic: Three reasons bind me to you for life."

sentences.zh: 將軍連年攻戰，軍糧苦少，今送米二十萬斛。

translations.literal: The general campaigns year after year and bitterly lacks grain; now I send two hundred thousand hu of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Your armies need grain—here are two hundred thousand hu."

sentences.zh: 非唯此止，當駱驛复致。

translations.literal: Not only this—more will arrive in steady succession.
translations.idiomatic: "More will follow without cease."

sentences.zh: 凡所短長亦唯命。

translations.literal: Whatever strengths or flaws—I await command.
translations.idiomatic: "Command me in all things."

sentences.zh: 」布得書大悅，即勒兵襲下邳，獲備妻子。

translations.literal: " Bu received the letter and was greatly pleased; he immediately mobilized troops to surprise Xiapi and seized Bei's wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu delighted in the flattery, stormed Xiapi, and captured Liu Bei's family.

sentences.zh: 備敗走海西，飢困，請降於布。

translations.literal: Bei fled defeated toward Haixi, starving and distressed, and asked to surrender to Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei fled to Haixi half starved and sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 布又恚術運糧不復至，乃具車馬迎備，以為豫州刺史，遣屯小沛。

translations.literal: Bu again resented that Shu's grain never arrived; he then prepared carriages and horses to welcome Bei, made him inspector of Yu Province, and sent him to encamp at Xiaopei.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shu's grain failed to appear, Lü Bu welcomed Liu Bei back, named him inspector of Yu, and parked him at Xiaopei.

sentences.zh: 布自號徐州牧。

translations.literal: Bu styled himself shepherd of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed the shepherdcy of Xu himself.

sentences.zh: 術懼布為己害，為子求婚，布复許之。

translations.literal: Shu feared Bu would harm him; he arranged a marriage proposal for his son; Bu again consented.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Lü Bu, Yuan Shu proposed a marriage and Lü Bu accepted again.

sentences.zh: 術遣將紀靈等步騎三萬以攻備，備求救於布。

translations.literal: Shu sent generals Ji Ling and others with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Bei; Bei begged rescue from Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu dispatched Ji Ling with thirty thousand men against Liu Bei, who cried to Lü Bu for help.

sentences.zh: 諸將謂布曰：「將軍常欲殺劉備，今可假手於術。

translations.literal: The generals said to Bu: "The general always wished to kill Liu Bei—now you may borrow Shu's hand."
translations.idiomatic: His officers said, "You always wanted Liu Bei dead—let Yuan Shu do it."

sentences.zh: 」布曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Bu said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: "No," said Lü Bu.

sentences.zh: 術若破備，則北連太山，吾為在術圍中，不得不救也。

translations.literal: If Shu destroys Bei, he will link north with Mount Tai—I will sit inside Shu's ring and cannot fail to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: "If Yuan Shu destroys Liu Bei he joins Taishan—I would be encircled."

sentences.zh: 」便率步騎千餘，馳往赴之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he led over a thousand infantry and cavalry and galloped to aid.
translations.idiomatic: He rode out with a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 靈等聞布至，皆斂兵而止。

translations.literal: When Ling and the others heard Bu had arrived, they all folded arms and halted.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Ling halted at news of his approach.

sentences.zh: 布屯沛城外，遣人招備，並請靈等與共饗飲。

translations.literal: Bu encamped outside Pei city, sent men to summon Bei, and invited Ling and company to drink together.
translations.idiomatic: He camped outside Pei, called Liu Bei in, and invited Ji Ling to parley.

sentences.zh: 布謂靈曰：「玄德，布弟也，為諸君所困，故來救之。

translations.literal: Bu said to Ling: "Xuan De is Bu's younger brother—trapped by you gentlemen, therefore I come to save him.
translations.idiomatic: "Xuan De is my sworn brother; you besieged him, so I came."

sentences.zh: 布性不喜合鬬，但喜解鬬耳。

translations.literal: Bu's nature does not delight in joining quarrels—only in settling quarrels.
translations.idiomatic: I dislike stirring fights—I prefer ending them."

sentences.zh: 」乃令軍候植戟於營門，布彎弓顧曰：「諸君觀布謝戟小支，中者當各解兵，不中可留決鬬。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ordered the army clerk to plant halberds at the camp gate; Bu bent his bow and looked back: "Gentlemen, watch Bu excuse the halberd's lower branch—whoever hits may stand down; whoever misses may fight it out.
translations.idiomatic: He had halberds planted at the gate and declared, "If my arrow strikes the halberd's fork, you stand down; if not, fight on."

sentences.zh: 」布即一發，正中戟支。

translations.literal: " Bu loosed once and struck the halberd fork squarely.
translations.idiomatic: His shot rang true.

sentences.zh: 靈等皆驚，言「將軍天威也」。

translations.literal: Ling and the others were astonished, saying "the general's heaven-sent majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Ji Ling gasped, "Heaven backs you!"

sentences.zh: 明日復歡會，然後各罷。

translations.literal: The next day they feasted happily again, then each withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They feasted again next day and dispersed.

sentences.zh: 術遣韓胤以僭號事告布，因求迎婦，布遣女隨之。

translations.literal: Shu sent Han Yin to inform Bu of his usurped title and seek to welcome the bride; Bu sent his daughter to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu sent Han Yin with news of his imperial claim to fetch the bride; Lü Bu sent his daughter along.

sentences.zh: 沛相陳珪恐術報布成姻，則徐、楊合從，為難未已。

translations.literal: Chancellor of Pei Chen Gui feared that if Shu repaid Bu by sealing marriage, Xu and Yang would league north-south—disaster unending.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gui feared a Xu–Yang alliance if the wedding closed.

sentences.zh: 於是往說布曰：「曹公奉迎天子，輔贊國政，將軍宜與協助同策謀，共存大計。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went to persuade Bu: "Lord Cao welcomes the Son of Heaven and assists state affairs—the general ought to join in counsel and share great plans.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Lü Bu to stand with Cao Cao, who held the emperor.

sentences.zh: 今與袁術結姻，必受不義之名，將有累卵之危矣。

translations.literal: Now if you bind marriage with Yuan Shu, you will surely receive an unrighteous name and face peril stacked like eggs.
translations.idiomatic: Tying yourself to Yuan Shu brands you traitor and invites ruin."

sentences.zh: 」布亦素怨術，而女已在塗，乃追還絕婚，執胤送許，曹操殺之。

translations.literal: " Bu also long resented Shu; his daughter was already on the road—he pursued her back, broke the marriage, seized Yin and sent him to Xu—Cao Cao executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu hated Yuan Shu anyway; he recalled the bridal train, broke the betrothal, handed Han Yin to Xu, and Cao Cao executed him.

sentences.zh: 陳珪欲使子登詣曹操，布固不許，會使至，拜布為左將軍，布大喜，即聽登行，並令奉章謝恩。

translations.literal: Chen Gui wished to send his son Deng to Cao Cao; Bu firmly refused—when an envoy arrived appointing Bu General of the Left, Bu was greatly pleased and immediately allowed Deng to go, ordering him to present memorial thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gui wanted Chen Deng to visit Cao Cao; Lü Bu refused until an edict named him General of the Left—then he sent Chen Deng with tribute.

sentences.zh: 登見曹操，因陳布勇而無謀，輕於去就，宜早圖之。

translations.literal: Deng saw Cao Cao and laid out that Bu was brave but witless, light in loyalty—he should be seized early.
