translations.idiomatic: Chen Deng warned Cao Cao that Lü Bu was brave, faithless, and should be removed soon.

sentences.zh: 操曰：「布狼子野心，誠難久養，非卿莫究其情偽。

translations.literal: Cao said: "Bu has a wolf cub's wild heart—truly hard to nurture long; none but you can probe truth and falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: "Lü Bu is ravenous as a wolf pup—hard to keep; only you read him."

sentences.zh: 」即增珪秩中二千石，拜登廣陵太守。

translations.literal: " He immediately raised Gui's salary to two thousand shi and promoted Deng to governor of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He raised Chen Gui's stipend and made Chen Deng governor of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 臨別，操執登手曰：「東方之事，便以相付。

translations.literal: At parting Cao grasped Deng's hand: "Eastern affairs I entrust to you.
translations.idiomatic: At farewell he gripped Chen Deng's hand: "The east is yours."

sentences.zh: 」令陰合部眾，以為內應。

translations.literal: " He ordered secret league with troops as inner collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: "Secretly rally allies against him."

sentences.zh: 始布因登求徐州牧，不得。

translations.literal: Earlier Bu through Deng had sought shepherd of Xu Province and did not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu had asked Chen Deng to win him Xu shepherd—unsuccessfully.

sentences.zh: 登還，布怒，拔戟斫机曰：「卿父勸吾協同曹操，絕婚公路。

translations.literal: Deng returned; Bu was angry, drew halberd and hacked the table: "Your father urged me to cooperate with Cao Cao and break marriage with Gonglu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Deng returned; Lü Bu smashed the table: "Your father pushed me toward Cao Cao and away from Yuan Shu."

sentences.zh: 今吾所求無獲，而卿父子並顯重，但為卿所賣耳。

translations.literal: Now what I sought I did not gain, yet you father and son together enjoy heavy rank—I am merely sold by you.
translations.idiomatic: I gained nothing while you two prosper—you sold me."

sentences.zh: 」登不為動容，徐對之曰：「登見曹公，言養將軍譬如養虎，當飽其肉，不飽則將噬人。

translations.literal: " Deng did not change expression; slowly he replied: "When Deng saw Lord Cao, I said raising the general is like raising a tiger—one must feed it meat; if not full it will devour men.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Deng calmly said he had told Cao Cao that backing Lü Bu was like feeding a tiger.

sentences.zh: 公曰：'不如卿言。

translations.literal: The lord said: "Not as you say.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao replied, "Not so.

sentences.zh: 譬如養鷹，飢即為用，飽則颺去。

translations.literal: It is like raising a hawk—hungry it serves you; full it flies away.
translations.idiomatic: Think of a hawk: keep it hungry and it serves you; feed it and it leaves.

sentences.zh: '其言如此。

translations.literal: " His words were thus.
translations.idiomatic: "That was his answer."

sentences.zh: 」布意乃解。

translations.literal: " Bu's intent then eased.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu cooled down.

sentences.zh: 袁術怒布殺韓胤，遣其大將張勛、橋蕤等與韓暹、楊奉連勢，步騎數万，七道攻布。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu was angry Bu killed Han Yin; he sent great generals Zhang Xun, Qiao Rui, and others with Han Xian and Yang Feng joining forces—several tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry in seven columns to attack Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged by Han Yin's death, Yuan Shu hurled Zhang Xun, Qiao Rui, Han Xian, and Yang Feng at Lü Bu in seven columns.

sentences.zh: 布時兵有三千，馬四百匹，懼其不敵，謂陳珪曰：「今致術軍，卿之由也，為之奈何？

translations.literal: Bu had three thousand troops and four hundred horses at the time; he feared they could not match; he said to Chen Gui: "Now Shu's army comes—this is your doing; what can be done?
translations.idiomatic: With only three thousand men Lü Bu blamed Chen Gui: "You brought this army—what now?"

sentences.zh: 」珪曰：「暹、奉與術，卒合之師耳。

translations.literal: " Gui said: "Xian and Feng with Shu are a hastily joined host.
translations.idiomatic: "Han Xian and Yang Feng are Yuan Shu's hired guns."

sentences.zh: 謀無素定，不能相維。

translations.literal: Their plans were never settled beforehand—they cannot sustain one another.
translations.idiomatic: They share no plan—they will not hold."

sentences.zh: 子登策之，比於連雞，勢不俱棲，立可離也。

translations.literal: Your son Deng calculates them as chickens roped together—they cannot perch together; they can be split at once.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Deng says they are chickens tied on one line—they scatter easy."

sentences.zh: 」布用珪策，與暹、奉書曰：「二將軍親拔大駕，而布手殺董卓，俱立功名，當垂竹帛。

translations.literal: " Bu used Gui's strategy and wrote Xian and Feng: "You two generals personally rescued the great carriage while Bu slew Dong Zhuo with his own hand—you both raised merit and should be inscribed on bamboo and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu wrote: "You rescued the emperor; I killed Dong Zhuo—we all served Han."

sentences.zh: 今袁術造逆，宜共誅討，奈何與賊還來伐布？

translations.literal: Now Yuan Shu rebels—ought we not jointly punish him? Why instead join the rebel to strike Bu?
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu rebels—why march with him against me?"

sentences.zh: 可因今者同力破術，為國除害，建功天下，此時不可失也。

translations.literal: You may now strike Shu together with me, rid the state of harm, and win merit under heaven—this moment must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Join me now, strike Yuan Shu, win glory—do not miss it."

sentences.zh: 」又許破術兵，悉以軍資與之。

translations.literal: " He further promised that when Shu's troops were broken, all military supplies would go to them.
translations.idiomatic: He promised them Yuan Shu's baggage train.

sentences.zh: 暹、奉大喜，遂共擊勳等於下邳，大破之，生禽橋蕤，餘眾潰走，其所殺傷、墯水死者殆盡。

translations.literal: Xian and Feng were greatly pleased; thereupon together they struck Xun and others at Xiapi, routed them greatly, captured Qiao Rui alive; the rest fled in rout—those killed, wounded, or drowned were nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: They turned on Yuan Shu's army at Xiapi, shattered it, took Qiao Rui alive, and slaughtered the rest.

sentences.zh: 時，太山臧霸等攻破莒城，許布財幣以相結，而未及送，布乃自往求之。

translations.literal: At that time Zang Ba of Mount Tai and others had broken Julu city; they promised Bu treasure to league together but had not yet delivered—Bu thereupon went in person to demand it.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Ba had promised him loot from Ju; Lü Bu went to collect.

sentences.zh: 其督將高順諫止曰：「將軍威名宣播，遠近所畏，何求不得，而自行求賂。

translations.literal: His supervising general Gao Shun remonstrated to stop him: "The general's awesome name spreads far—near and far fear you; what could you not obtain, yet you go in person to beg bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shun warned: "Your name terrifies the region—why demean yourself chasing silver?"

sentences.zh: 萬一不克，豈不損邪？

translations.literal: If by chance you do not overcome—is it not damage?
translations.idiomatic: "What if you fail?"

sentences.zh: 」布不從。

translations.literal: " Bu did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu ignored him.

sentences.zh: 既至莒，霸等不測往意，固守拒之，無獲而還。

translations.literal: When he reached Ju, Ba and the others could not fathom his intent; they firmly defended and refused him—he gained nothing and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Ju, Zang Ba could not read his purpose and shut the gates; Lü Bu marched home empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 順為人清白有威嚴，少言辭，將眾整齊，每戰必克。

translations.literal: Shun as a man was pure and stern, sparing of speech; he commanded troops in tight order and invariably prevailed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shun was austere and disciplined—few words, crack formations, victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 布性決易，所為無常。

translations.literal: Bu's nature was impulsive and erratic—his conduct lacked constancy.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu was mercurial—no steady judgment.

sentences.zh: 順每諫曰：「將軍舉動，不肯詳思，忽有失得，動輒言誤。

translations.literal: Shun often remonstrated: "The general's movements—you refuse careful reflection; suddenly gain or loss shifts, and at every turn your words miss the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shun urged him: "You rush every choice without thinking—you blunder and blame fate."

sentences.zh: 誤事豈可數乎？

translations.literal: Can mistaken deeds be countless?
translations.idiomatic: "How often can you afford mistakes?"

sentences.zh: 」布知其忠而不能從。

translations.literal: " Bu knew his loyalty yet could not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu knew he was right—and ignored him.

sentences.zh: 建安三年，布遂復從袁術，遣順攻劉備於沛，破之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jian'an, Bu again attached to Yuan Shu; he sent Shun to attack Liu Bei at Pei and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In 198 Lü Bu renewed ties with Yuan Shu and sent Gao Shun to crush Liu Bei at Pei.

sentences.zh: 曹操遣夏侯惇救備，為順所敗。

translations.literal: Cao Cao sent Xiahou Dun to rescue Bei; Dun was defeated by Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's relief column under Xiahou Dun fell to Gao Shun.

sentences.zh: 操乃自將擊布，至下邳城下。

translations.literal: Cao thereupon personally led troops to strike Bu and reached beneath Xiapi's walls.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao then invested Xiapi in person.

sentences.zh: 遺布書，為陳禍福。

translations.literal: He sent Bu a letter laying out fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote outlining Lü Bu's choices.

sentences.zh: 布欲降，而陳宮等自以負罪於操，深沮其計，而謂布曰：「曹公遠來，勢不能久。

translations.literal: Bu wished to surrender, but Chen Gong and others, considering themselves guilty toward Cao, deeply thwarted his plan and said to Bu: "Lord Cao has come from afar—his momentum cannot last long.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu considered surrender; Chen Gong, fearing Cao Cao's vengeance, blocked him: "Cao Cao came a long way—he cannot endure."

sentences.zh: 將軍若以步騎出屯於外，宮將餘眾閉守於內。

translations.literal: If the general leads infantry and cavalry out to encamp outside, Gong will close the remainder inside and hold fast.
translations.idiomatic: "You sortie with the horse; I seal the city."

sentences.zh: 若向將軍，宮引兵而攻其背；

translations.literal: If they turn toward the general, Gong will lead troops and strike their rear.
translations.idiomatic: "If he turns on you, I strike his rear."

sentences.zh: 若但攻城，則將軍救於外。

translations.literal: If they only assault the city, then the general relieves from outside.
translations.idiomatic: "If he only besieges me, you relieve from without."

sentences.zh: 不過旬月，軍食畢盡，擊之可破也。

translations.literal: Within no more than ten months their army grain will be exhausted—strike then and you can break them.
translations.idiomatic: "Inside two months his supplies fail—then we crush him."

sentences.zh: 」布然之。

translations.literal: " Bu approved.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu agreed.

sentences.zh: 布妻曰：「昔曹氏待公檯如赤子，猶舍而歸我。

translations.literal: Bu's wife said: "Formerly the Cao clan treated Lord Gongtai like an infant—yet he left them and returned to us.
translations.idiomatic: His wife objected: "Cao Cao once cherished Chen Gong like a child—yet Gong abandoned him for you."

sentences.zh: 今將軍厚公檯不過於曹氏，而欲委全城，捐妻、子，孤軍遠出乎？

translations.literal: Now the general favors Lord Gongtai no more than the Cao clan did—yet you wish to entrust the whole city, abandon wife and children, and march out alone with an isolated army?
translations.idiomatic: "You hardly favor Gong more than Cao did—would you abandon your walls, wife, and children on one reckless ride?"

sentences.zh: 若一旦有變，妾豈得為將軍妻哉！

translations.literal: If once there is a turn of fate, could your concubine remain the general's wife!
translations.idiomatic: "If disaster strikes, will I still be your wife?"

sentences.zh: 」布乃止。

translations.literal: " Bu thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 而潛遣人求救於袁術，自將千餘騎出。

translations.literal: Yet secretly he sent men to beg rescue from Yuan Shu; personally he led over a thousand riders out.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly begged Yuan Shu while leading a thousand riders out himself.

sentences.zh: 戰敗走還，保城不敢出。

translations.literal: Defeated in battle he fled back and defended the city, not daring to emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Beaten, he fled behind the walls and dared not sortie.

sentences.zh: 術亦不能救。

translations.literal: Shu also could not save him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu could not break the siege.

sentences.zh: 曹操塹圍之，壅沂、泗以灌其城，三月，上下離心。

translations.literal: Cao Cao dug trenches encircling him, dammed Yi and Si to flood the city; by the third month high and low were estranged at heart.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao ringed Xiapi with ditches and drowned it from the Yi and Si—by the third month garrison and townsfolk had turned on Lü Bu.

sentences.zh: 其將侯成使客牧其名馬，而客策之以叛。

translations.literal: His general Hou Cheng had a client herd his famous horse; the client whipped it away in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Cheng's groom stole his prized stallion.

sentences.zh: 成追客得馬，諸將合禮以賀成。

translations.literal: Cheng pursued the client and recovered the horse; the generals jointly observed ritual to congratulate Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Cheng recovered it; the officers toasted his luck.

sentences.zh: 成分酒肉，先入詣布而言曰：「蒙將軍威靈，得所亡馬，諸將齊賀，未敢嘗也，故先以奉貢。

translations.literal: Cheng divided wine and meat, first entered to visit Bu and said: "Thanks to the general's awesome might we recovered the lost horse; the generals jointly congratulate—I dare not taste first; therefore I present this offering first.
translations.idiomatic: He brought wine and meat to Lü Bu first: "Your might restored my horse—the men feast but I bring you the first cup."

sentences.zh: 」布怒曰：「布禁酒而卿等醖釀，為欲因酒共謀布邪？

translations.literal: " Bu angrily said: "Bu forbade wine yet you brew fermentation—do you wish by wine together to plot Bu?
translations.idiomatic: "I banned liquor and you brew—plotting against me?"

sentences.zh: 」成忿懼，乃與諸將共執陳宮、高順，率其眾降。

translations.literal: " Cheng resentful and afraid, then together with the generals seized Chen Gong and Gao Shun and led their hosts to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated and frightened, Hou Cheng bound Chen Gong and Gao Shun and opened the gates.

sentences.zh: 布與麾下登白門樓。

translations.literal: Bu with his household climbed White Gate Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu fled to White Gate Tower with his family.

sentences.zh: 兵圍之急，令左右取其首詣操。

translations.literal: With troops pressing the siege urgently, he ordered those about him to take his head to Cao.
translations.idiomatic: As the cord tightened he ordered someone to deliver his head to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 左右不忍，乃下降。

translations.literal: Those about him could not bear it; then they descended in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: His men refused and surrendered instead.

sentences.zh: 布見操曰：「今日已往，天下定矣。

translations.literal: Bu seeing Cao said: "From this day forward the realm is settled.
translations.idiomatic: Before Cao Cao he boasted, "From today the empire is decided."

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「何以言之？

translations.literal: " Cao said: "Why do you say so?
translations.idiomatic: "How so?"

sentences.zh: 」布曰：「明公之所患不過於布，今已服矣。

translations.literal: " Bu said: "What my lord feared was none other than Bu—now Bu has submitted.
translations.idiomatic: "You feared only me—and I yield."

sentences.zh: 令布將騎，明公將步，天下不足定也。

translations.literal: Let Bu command cavalry and my lord infantry—the realm is not enough to be settled.
translations.idiomatic: "Give me the horse and you the foot—the realm falls."

sentences.zh: 」顧謂劉備曰：「玄德，卿為坐上客，我為降虜，繩縛我急，獨不可一言邪？

translations.literal: " Looking toward Liu Bei he said: "Xuan De—you are guest of honor seated; I am captive surrendered—why bind me so tightly—will you not speak one word?
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Liu Bei: "Xuan De, you sit honored—I hang bound; won't you plead?"

sentences.zh: 」操笑曰：「縛虎不得不急。

translations.literal: " Cao smiled and said: "Binding a tiger cannot but be tight.
translations.idiomatic: "Tigers must be tied tight."

sentences.zh: 」乃令緩布縛。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ordered Bu's bonds loosened.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the ropes slackened.

sentences.zh: 劉備曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Liu Bei said: "It cannot be.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei said no.

sentences.zh: 明公不見呂布事丁建陽、董太師乎？

translations.literal: Does my lord not see Bu's service to Ding Jianyang and Grand Tutor Dong?
translations.idiomatic: "Remember Ding Yuan and Dong Zhuo?"

sentences.zh: 」操頷之。

translations.literal: " Cao nodded.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao nodded.

sentences.zh: 布目備曰：「大耳兒最叵信！

translations.literal: Bu glared at Bei and said: "That big-eared boy—least trustworthy of all!
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu snarled at Liu Bei, "Big-eared bastard—least trustworthy alive!"

sentences.zh: 」操謂陳宮曰：「公檯平生自謂智有餘，今意何如？

translations.literal: " Cao said to Chen Gong: "Lord Gongtai all your life called yourself more than wise enough—what now of your intent?
translations.idiomatic: "Chen Gong, you called yourself clever—how now?"

sentences.zh: 」宮指布曰：「是子不用宮言，以至於此。

translations.literal: " Gong pointed at Bu and said: "This fellow did not use Gong's words—thereby reaching this.
translations.idiomatic: "He never listened—that is why."

sentences.zh: 若見從，未可量也。

translations.literal: If he had followed my counsel, the outcome could not have been measured.
translations.idiomatic: "Had he obeyed, who knows how high we might have risen?"

sentences.zh: 」操又曰：「奈卿老母何？

translations.literal: " Cao again said: "What of your aged mother?
translations.idiomatic: "And your mother?"

sentences.zh: 」宮曰：「老母在公，不在宮也。

translations.literal: " Gong said: "The aged mother rests with you, not with Gong.
translations.idiomatic: "Her fate rests with you, not me."

sentences.zh: 夫以孝理天下者，不害人之親。

translations.literal: He who orders the realm by filial piety does not harm others' kin.
translations.idiomatic: "A king who rules through filial piety does not murder mothers."

sentences.zh: 」操復曰：「奈卿妻、子何？

translations.literal: " Cao again said: "What of your wife and children?
translations.idiomatic: "Your wife and children?"

sentences.zh: 」宮曰：「宮聞霸王之主，不絕人之祀。

translations.literal: " Gong said: "Gong has heard that hegemon kings do not cut off others' sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: "True kings end no family line."

sentences.zh: 」固請就刑，遂出不顧，操為之泣涕。

translations.literal: " He firmly requested execution, then went out without looking back; Cao wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: He demanded death and walked away; Cao Cao wept.

sentences.zh: 布及宮、順皆縊殺之，傳首許市。

translations.literal: Bu together with Gong and Shun were all strangled to death; their heads were sent to the market at Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu, Chen Gong, and Gao Shun were strangled; their heads went to Xu.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：焉作庸牧，以希後福。

translations.literal: Encomium says: Yan became a regional shepherd, hoping for later blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Liu Yan sought fortune as shepherd.

sentences.zh: 曷云負荷？

translations.literal: What of bearing the burden?
translations.idiomatic: Could he bear the weight?

sentences.zh: 地墮身逐。

translations.literal: Earth slipped—body driven forth.
translations.idiomatic: Ground gave way and swept him away.

sentences.zh: 術既叨貪，布亦翻覆。

translations.literal: Shu was grasping and greedy; Bu too turned coat again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu devoured everything; Lü Bu betrayed every master.
